questions.stem: If a lexer processes 1000 characters in 0.5 seconds, what is its processing speed in characters per second?
questions.explanation: The processing speed is calculated by dividing the total number of characters by the time taken. Thus, 1000 characters / 0.5 seconds = 2000 characters per second.

questions.stem: Explain how a lexer distinguishes between keywords and identifiers.
markingGuide: Keywords are predefined and reserved words in a language.
Identifiers are user-defined names for variables, functions, etc.
The lexer checks if a sequence of characters matches a keyword list.
If not a keyword, the sequence is treated as an identifier.
questions.explanation: A lexer distinguishes keywords from identifiers by checking if the character sequence matches any reserved words in the language. If it matches, it is a keyword; otherwise, it is treated as an identifier.

questions.stem: Describe the advantages of using a table-driven lexer over a hand-written lexer.
markingGuide: Table-driven lexers are systematic and easier to modify.
They separate the logic of state transitions from the code.
Easier to maintain and extend for new tokens.
Can be generated automatically from formal specifications.
questions.explanation: Table-driven lexers offer a structured approach that separates state logic from code, making them easier to modify and extend. They can be generated from formal specifications, providing flexibility and maintainability over hand-written lexers.
